_comment: Load gate for tests/load/run.py. Measurements themselves are accumulated per version
in docs/perf.md, which also records the hardware each number came from.
max_p95_ratio is the *regression* gate, and it is deliberately tighter than the 1.2x
figure the documentation promises. Three consecutive runs on ubuntu-24.04 against
MySQL 8.4.11 measured 0.874 to 0.911 at 300k rows and 1, 8 and 32 sessions: GCM is
faster than the CBC builtin on this workload, so a 1.2 gate could never fire and a
doubling of per-row cost would pass unnoticed. The ratio is also the noise-immune
metric — it normalises away runner speed, and its own run-to-run spread was 1.04x —
which is why it is the number that can be tightened rather than the absolute one.
max_p95_ms_at_largest_serial stays at the 1s promise from docs/design.md. Observed:
244 to 266 ms. It is an absolute ceiling on a shared runner, so tightening it would
buy sensitivity at the price of failures that say nothing about this component.
Raising either number needs a PR that states the hardware, the server version and why
the regression is acceptable, and updates docs/perf.md in the same change.
